summary: Milestone 2k drives the two in-mission HUD screens whose update virtual is reconstructed. The interface request now carries the controlled unit, so the recovered 20h arm classifies it as a ship and publishes 25h INTF_CAPTAIN's level-1 set, which raises the markers screen (4Dh) and keeps the minimap (35h); the recovered pump 004f8830 then calls 005c0f20 and 006435d0 every frame. The minimap places one icon per unit that survives the recovered filters, at the camera-relative rotated position 005c1b62 computes, with the two radii read out of the installed globals.lua. The markers pass runs end to end over a documented stand-in camera and adds the one marker its own selection produces.

The squad arm never runs: its list is the world object's and the radius at unit+7C4h has no recovered field, so hud_marker_within_radius rejects every mate.

The parts object belongs to packet unit_parts; a created instance has none, so the gate answers the value that lets the unit through and the record says so.
bsp/unit_instance.hpp carries +5Ch and +5Dh; +5Eh and +60h have no field and are treated as the clear a created instance leaves them at.
The ship probe, IsKindOf(5), is the branch the mission's destroyers take.

The non-objective part of the rule is run in the executable to choose which of the six colour templates a minimap icon is cloned from; the objective arm needs an objective container this process does not build.
bsp::hud_markers_add_unit_marker_006430c0 runs the whole rule.
The per-marker widget writer has no reconstruction, so the executable clones the page's own sidemarker_Group and places the clone from the screen bounds.
Unit_name_Text is filled with a plain C string, not a localisation id; the executable's text path only carries ids, so the label keeps the page's authored `Unit Name` and nothing invents a string.
STAND-IN: no camera exists, so the projection is a fixed top-down orthographic camera fitted to the mission's own unit bounds.
Part of the same stand-in.

corrections.was: docs/GAME_EXECUTABLE.md milestone 2h: 'the executable applies exactly that id rather than choosing one', with the null payload Init pushes.
corrections.is: That is right for Init's own request and wrong as the mission's final state. The 20h arm with a payload is a unit-kind classifier; with the controlled unit it re-enters its own virtual +10h with 25h INTF_CAPTAIN, whose level-1 set is 29h 49h 44h 27h 4Dh 45h 46h 26h 2Eh 35h 50h.
corrections.evidence: docs/IN_GAME_INTERFACE_SCREEN_SETS.md's 20h table and its 25h row; the run log's two 'in-mission level-1 set' lines.

corrections.was: This packet's brief: 'the world-to-minimap transform from the mission's map bounds'.
corrections.is: The transform is camera-relative and camera-rotated. 00432650's +6Ch and +70h are Minimap.MinimapRange and Minimap.VisibilityRange, both 4000, and docs/HUD_MINIMAP.md's own correction says neither is a map bound. The mission's bounds play no part in the minimap; they are only the stand-in marker camera's.

corrections.was: docs/MOTION_DIFFERENTIAL.md and milestone 2j: the executable and src/ship_motion_probe.cpp agree to 0.0005 degrees of heading over 14 s.
corrections.is: They no longer do, and the executable is the side that lags. Commit 4977f563 gave the probe the hull body 00937c90's tail creates and the dynamics world 004ddb90 fills, so the probe applies the body's angular damping and settles at 0.05513 rad/s, while this executable still leaves the body without mass, inertia or damping and settles at 0.06109. The executable's own numbers are unchanged from milestone 2j's published run, so nothing here regressed; what is missing is the same hull-body creation on the executable's side.
corrections.evidence: bsp_ship_motion_probe.exe --class 20 --throttle 1 --rudder 1 prints 'peak yaw rate 0.05513 ... the hull's angular damping (rate 1.0, twice per substep) scales that target by 0.9025'; the run log's 'controlled unit frame 280 ... yaw=-0.06109'.

corrections.was: This packet's brief: cruise, 'when cc_cruise_command is on main'.
corrections.is: It is not on main as of 2b6cce8b, so the authored Cruise token is still turned into one order of throttle 1 and rudder 0 by milestone 2i's own decision. A run with no --order still moves all 32 ships; the ordered pair each unit runs under is now a column of the end-of-run distance table.
corrections.evidence: git log --oneline main; the 'unit throttle rudder' table in the run log of a --mission-frames 300 run with no --order.

corrections.was: docs/GAME_EXECUTABLE.md milestone 2b: the sprite bridge 'orders quads back to front by the authored Z alone'.
corrections.is: Still true for authored widgets, and this milestone shows the rule is not the game's: GUI_minimap puts its island map at Z -5 and its frame, glass and direction wedge at -22, -23 and -24, so a Z-only order draws the frame over the unit icons, while the page's geOrder puts unit_marker_Group (0) in front of all of them. geOrder is not a draw order either (sidemarker_Group gives HP_Icon 5 and HP_BG_Icon 3), so the bridge keeps the Z rule for authored widgets and adds one rule for the widgets the executable created.
